description: The Cook Islands LiDAR Project gives the Cook Islands their first precise three-dimensional measurement of land and near-shore seabed, launched on 25 September 2026 under the theme "Mapping Our Islands, Shaping Our Future". The Office of the Prime Minister article read on 2026-09-28 says the project was implemented by Infrastructure Cook Islands with support from the Green Climate Fund, New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the government, with Earth Science New Zealand as technical partner, and delivered high-resolution digital elevation and surface models, imagery and topobathymetry; flood-catchment hazard mapping for different rainfall and flood magnitudes including climate change scenarios and flood risk to infrastructure and key assets; coastal and tidal inundation mapping with sea level rise scenarios identifying vulnerable infrastructure; and GIS training. Coverage is national. Access is through the CookGeo Portal, a national platform for agencies, technical teams and partners; public terms and licence are not stated. Caveats: public availability is unclear and the portal was not read. It supports hazard exposure and adaptation planning of roads, drainage, culverts and coastal assets. Related records: data-cook-islands-environment-data-portal holds other national environmental data.
